title: A Regiment for the Harbor
premise: Orsen Amberdale, a pearl diver's son indentured to the Vellamare Trading Company's harbor workshop, has survived twelve years by being forgettable—until an abandoned child arrives at his door with a note instructing him to forget her face. The girl, Sefi, carries a pearl pendant that matches one Orsen's drowned mother once wore, tying her to the inheritance Orsen was made to surrender when he signed his indenture papers. As he secretly investigates the child's origins, he uncovers that the company has been laundering stolen heirloom pearls through its workshop and erasing the families they came from—including his own. When the workshop's ledger-burner comes to destroy the evidence and Sefi with it, Orsen must choose between the safety of invisibility and claiming his name; he exposes the trade at the harbor's pearl auction, saves Sefi, and ends the novel not as a company asset but as keeper of his mother's restored workshop, with Sefi as the first apprentice of a new, honest registry.
about_author: Paloma Oyelaran is a former archivist who spent years cataloguing maritime trade records from coastal port cities, where she became fascinated by the unnamed laborers between the lines of ledgers. She writes historical fiction about people history tried to make invisible.

chapters.title: The Weight of Being Unremarked
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A day in the Vellamare workshop establishes his careful choreography of silence: how he sorts pearls without looking at their owners' names, how he deflects the overseer's attention. The emotional beat is the ache of competence without identity—he is excellent at work designed to erase him.

chapters.title: A Bundle Against the Door
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, night. He finds a sleeping child on his doorstep with a note: 'Forget the face.' Instinct says report her; instead he hides her in the loft above the drying racks. The beat is terror warring with a recognition he can't name—the child clutches a pearl pendant like his mother's.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Does Not Say
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He falsifies a supply entry to account for extra rations while studying old indenture rolls for Sefi's origins. He finds his own entry: 'Amberdale boy, no kin claimed.' The beat is quiet fury—his erasure was paperwork, deliberate and routine.

chapters.title: The Diver's Daughter
chapters.summary: Sefi's POV, fragmentary and childlike. She remembers fragments: a boat, singing, hands tearing the pendant from her neck before someone carried her away. The beat is heartbreak filtered through incomprehension—she doesn't know she was stolen, only that she was told to be quiet.

chapters.title: Salt and Signatures
chapters.summary: Orsen visits retired diver Maren Oduya, who recognizes the pendant as a diving-family inheritance mark. She reveals the company buys pearls from desperate families, then burns the records proving ownership. The beat is dawning conspiracy: the silences Orsen kept were load-bearing walls.

chapters.title: The Man Who Burns Paper
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Ledger-burner Corvane Halst arrives to audit the workshop ahead of the auction season, and his questions circle uncomfortably near the loft. Orsen performs invisibility perfectly—and hates how good it still feels. The beat is dread sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, flashback woven through present. We learn how his mother drowned diving company waters after refusing to sell her inheritance pearls, and how the orphaned boy's indenture was the company's settlement. The beat is grief transmuted: he finally understands what he inherited—not pearls, but the debt of remembering.

chapters.title: Copies in Candle Oil
chapters.summary: Orsen and Maren secretly copy the true ownership records hidden behind the workshop's false wall, discovered via Sefi's pendant matching a sealed inventory lot. Halst nearly catches them; Sefi distracts him with practiced innocence. The beat is found family forged under pressure—three erased people building one testimony.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, climax. At the harbor's grand pearl auction, he steps onto the floor—an indentured boy has no voice there—and reads the true registry aloud as Maren's diver allies hold back Halst's men. The company's buyers recoil; the harbor master halts the sale. The beat is the terrifying, exhilarating cost of becoming visible.

chapters.title: A Registry of Names
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV, resolution. The workshop reopens under harbor authority with Orsen as keeper of a public ownership registry; his indenture voided, his mother's name restored to the rolls. He takes Sefi's hand and enters her as his first apprentice—under her real name, which they are still learning together. The beat is belonging chosen, not granted.
